t: A confederation of Germanic peoples on the upper Rhine and Danube, ruled by many separate kings rather than one.
After Rome abandoned the Limes around 260 they settled the lands of later Swabia, Alsace and northern Switzerland.
Defeated by Clovis I around 496–506, they became the Frankish Duchy of Alamannia; their dialects survive today.
dyk: The French word for Germany, Allemagne, and the Spanish Alemania come from the Alemanni, one people of the south-west, not from the Germans as a whole.
ev: Caracalla campaigns on the Main; Cassius Dio names the Alemanni
Rome abandons the Limes and the Alemanni begin to settle the Agri Decumates
Alemanni and Juthungi defeat Aurelian at Placentia before he destroys them
Julian defeats Chnodomar’s coalition at the Battle of Strasbourg
Valentinian I makes peace with King Macrianus on the Rhine near Mainz
Gratian’s army defeats the Lentienses at Argentaria in Alsace
Clovis I defeats the Alemanni, traditionally at Tolbiac
A second Frankish victory ends Alemannic independence

f.predecessor: Elbe Germanic peoples such as the Semnones (Suebi)
f.successor: Kingdom of the Franks (Duchy of Alamannia)
